per_dimension.notes: Actor filters for 'RU/UA state forces or affiliated groups' vary widely (broad keyword soups vs root-substring '%russ%/%ukrain%' and use of inter1/2 or actor1-only). Rosgvardia matching is consistent where explicitly targeted.
The definition of Russian border oblasts differs (3 vs 6 oblasts). Kursk oblast is matched with exact equality vs prefix matching in different places.
Most 2024 and Aug–Dec 2024 windows are aligned. One pre/post split for the Kursk incursion uses July 1 instead of August 1; other periods (full-2024; 2023–2024 span) are consistently bounded.

Definitions of 'cross-border strikes', 'civilian targeting', and 'Russian assault activity' differ across queries. Monthly distributions by event_type/sub_event_type within RU border oblasts are aligned.
Counts and fatality sums use consistent COUNT(*) and SUM semantics where the same concepts are measured. DISTINCT is used only where deduplication is necessary (Q0) and not reused elsewhere.

Some RU border queries omit country='Russia' while others include it. Queries claiming 'Russia–Ukraine conflict' sometimes include all events in those countries (no actor filters) and sometimes restrict to RU/UA forces.

conflicts.concept: RU/UA forces inclusion for RU/UA events (monthly series)
conflicts.predicate_a: AND (actor1 ILIKE '%Russia%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%Russian%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%Ukraine%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%Ukrainian%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%military%' OR ... OR actor2 ILIKE '%pro-Ukraine%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%Wagner%')
conflicts.predicate_b: AND (actor1 ILIKE '%russ%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%russ%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%ukrain%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%ukrain%')
conflicts.explanation: Q6 admits a much broader set (includes 'military', 'security forces', 'police', 'militia', 'Wagner', etc.), while Q10 only matches substrings 'russ'/'ukrain'. This will include/exclude different events under the same conceptual umbrella.

conflicts.concept: RU/UA forces inclusion for RU/UA events (2024 distributions)
conflicts.predicate_a: COALESCE(actor1,'') ILIKE ANY(ARRAY['%Ukraine%','%Ukrainian%','%Russia%','%Russian%','%State forces%','%Armed Forces%','%Military%','%National Guard%','%Border Guard%','%Rosgvard%','%FSB%','%Wagner%','%Kadyrov%','%Chechen%','%Volunteer%','%Territorial Defense%']) OR same for actor2
conflicts.predicate_b: actor1 ILIKE '%russ%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%russ%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%ukrain%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%ukrain%'
conflicts.explanation: Q8 includes many affiliated formations (FSB, Kadyrov, etc.) that Q10 would miss unless they contain 'russ'/'ukrain' substrings.

conflicts.concept: Russian assault/offensive presence in Ukrainian fronts
conflicts.predicate_a: actor1 ILIKE any of ('%Russia%','%Russian%','%Russian Armed Forces%','%Wagner%','%Akhmat%','%Chechen%','%Donetsk People%Republic%','%Luhansk People%Republic%','%DNR%','%LNR%') AND event_type IN ('Battles','Explosions/Remote violence','Strategic developments')
conflicts.predicate_b: (actor1 ILIKE '%Russia%' OR actor1 ILIKE '%Russian%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%Russia%' OR actor2 ILIKE '%Russian%') AND (event_type='Battles' OR sub_event_type IN ('Armed clash','Attack'))
conflicts.explanation: Q22 uses actor1-only and includes 'Strategic developments'; Q26 requires 'battlelike' events and allows actor2 to carry the Russian match. The resulting event sets differ materially.
Q16 treats only three oblasts as border oblasts, while Q17 broadens to six. Counts and trends are not comparable under the same 'border oblasts' label.
Prefix matching can include variants like 'Kursk Oblast'/'Kurskaya', while exact equality may miss them, yielding different row sets.

conflicts.concept: Pre/post split around Ukraine’s 2024 Kursk incursion
conflicts.predicate_a: CASE WHEN event_date >= DATE '2024-08-01' AND event_date <= DATE '2024-12-31' THEN 'post' ELSE 'pre' END
conflicts.predicate_b: CASE WHEN event_date < DATE '2024-07-01' THEN 'pre' ELSE 'post' END
conflicts.explanation: Q16 defines post as August–December 2024; Q18 defines post as July–December 2024. This shifts a full month between periods, altering comparisons.

conflicts.predicate_a: sub_event_type IN ('Air/drone strike','Shelling/artillery/missile attack') (Russia, admin1 IN ('Belgorod','Kursk','Bryansk'))
conflicts.predicate_b: No event_type restriction; events tagged as cross-border via actor/source/notes heuristics in UA border oblasts and RU border oblasts
conflicts.explanation: Q1 limits to specific remote-violence sub_event_types; Q17 includes any event types inferred as cross-border via notes/actors. Different taxonomies produce non-comparable series.
Q1’s civilian metric includes any VAC events and any civilian-targeted events; Q4 restricts to artillery/missile events that are civilian-targeted. The underlying event sets differ.
Q22 includes Strategic developments and remote violence; Q26 limits to battlelike forms only. These reflect different conceptual definitions of 'assault activity'.

conflicts.concept: Russia–Ukraine conflict scope (actors vs all events)
conflicts.predicate_a: country IN ('Ukraine','Russia') AND (actor1/actor2 contains RU/UA state forces or affiliates via keyword list)
conflicts.predicate_b: country IN ('Ukraine','Russia') AND event_type IS NOT NULL (no actor filter)
conflicts.explanation: Q8 restricts to conflict actors; Q9 includes all events in the two countries (e.g., protests, crime), yet both are framed as 'Russia–Ukraine conflict' aggregates.

conflicts.concept: RU border oblasts: ensuring Russian events only
conflicts.explanation: Q24 can pick up any rows with those admin1 names regardless of country coding, unlike Q16. Country omission risks including/excluding records inconsistently.

conflicts.concept: Kursk/Belgorod Aug–Dec 2024 infrastructure-adjacent events: country filter
conflicts.explanation: Q28 omits country='Russia' while Q15 requires it, yet both discuss RU oblasts. This can change which rows are counted if admin1 names appear under different country codings.

summary: The audit finds significant inconsistencies across actor filtering, geography sets, event taxonomy, and population scope. Most temporal windows are aligned, and counting/aggregation methods are coherent where the same concepts are measured, but several key comparisons (e.g., RU/UA actor inclusion, border oblast definitions, and cross-border/civilian-targeting taxonomies) use divergent predicates that would change results. Harmonizing these filters is necessary for mutually comparable figures.
